Sealed read plan said about 40 npm version docs; 71 were fetched because the lock closure has 71 packages. Total requests 133 of 160; the plan figures were not sealed expectations.
The first seal attempt failed inside the shell before any file was written (no side effect); the seal was then written by a script that refuses to overwrite. The sealed file is the only seal.

Helper revisions: rev1 (sha256 66f574eae2a35ab84f812d4bf4c44f70cf1e06c6b3f436838683d0c3889bfd5f) was authored after the seal and used for a selector prototype on the real lock and fixtures; rev2 (sha256 471408755290b1aa205e01b580cc18eb6e278b705701726046b030cd84f98939) is the final embedded helper (removed blank lines, fixed no-wheel bookkeeping, a regex that matched its own source, and an unclear SP-05 and SP-10 expression). Expectations were not changed; all checks were replayed on rev2.
The npm closure comes from a local approximation of bun nesting over bun.lock text; it was not validated against npm or bun.

Two HEAD or GET reads ended in redirects that were not followed: BtbN release asset (to an off-list release-assets host) and the gyan sha256 text (303). Hashes and sizes for those two come only from API or page declarations.
Historical comparison hashes for the three source repositories come from the tracked D107 evidence ledger, not from a local mirror; no mirror or index was read or touched in this run.

The required full worker-return gate exits 1 because the dispatched return path contains the excluded marker _COMPLETION_ (batch name METADATA_COMPLETION); the quality checker decides eligibility from the path alone. Not renamed, no checker changed; other gate stages pass and the return text diagnoses clean under a neutral probe path name (read-only call, informational).
Reads were bounded by the reader code (160 requests, 4 MiB per GET, 32 MiB total, no redirects, HEAD without body); this is a cooperative control, not an OS sandbox.
